basis: Defining fatty-acid oxidation defect, liver disease and cardiomyopathy; neuropathy/developmental delay 30-79%. Visual loss/abnormal ERG 30-79% omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral neuropathy and developmental impairment each occur in 30-79%; progressive neurologic disability retained at the cap.
decisions.ocular: none: visual loss and abnormal ERG occur in 30-79%, but omitted at four-axis cap in favor of progressive neurologic disability.

basis: Bacteria-associated granulomatous disease predominantly affecting urinary tract; skin inflammation/ulcers annotated 80-99%. Bowel symptoms do not establish common intestinal tissue damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal disease can occur, but ancestry and frequent diarrhea/abdominal pain do not establish direct intestinal lesions in at least 30% across the disease.

basis: Malignant tumor arising in the thyroid gland; endothelial histology does not establish additional cardiovascular organ damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thyroid is the anatomical tumor site; vascular differentiation alone does not establish disease of the heart or clinically affected vessels.

basis: Palmar fascial fibrosis and shortening cause permanent finger contractures; the defining lesion affects locomotor connective tissue.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the defining lesion is palmar fascia, despite the epidermal wording and skin ancestry; skin tethering does not establish a separate primary skin lesion.

basis: Developmental impairment, skeletal abnormalities and ocular malformations define the syndrome; eye hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and urinary anomalies occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular malformations explicitly characterize the syndrome in its definition; eye aplasia/hypoplasia is annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines the disease; nail abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Respiratory physiology abnormalities (30-79%) and hoarseness do not establish common direct airway damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: abnormal respiratory physiology occurs in 30-79%, but direct persistent airway injury is not established; bronchoconstriction has no frequency and hoarseness is a symptom.

basis: Developmental delay/intellectual disability and characteristic fifth-finger skeletal abnormalities occur in 4/4; cardiac and laryngeal defects each occur in 1/4, below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic fifth-digit skeletal abnormalities are a defining Coffin-Siris feature; clinodactyly occurs in all four reported CSS10 patients.

basis: Cataract, hypertrichosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; dental/palatal anomalies occur in 80-99%. Pectus excavatum, also 80-99%, omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: microdontia and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%; direct dental/oral malformations retained as the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus excavatum occurs in 80-99%, but omitted at four-axis cap; severity or associated cardiopulmonary impairment is not documented.

basis: Gut and marrow cytotoxicity; cardiac injury and renal failure each 30-79%. Encephalopathy (30-79%) and secondary acid-base/electrolyte derangements omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: renal insufficiency and oliguric renal failure occur in 30-79%; severe organ dysfunction retained at the cap.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acidosis (80-99%) and electrolyte abnormalities are secondary systemic derangements; severe cardiac and renal organ failure take priority at four-axis cap.

basis: Seizures and hemiparesis establish neurologic disease. Hemi­atrophy and unspecified skeletal abnormalities lack anatomical detail or frequency to establish another axis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: unspecified skeletal abnormality and hemiatrophy have no frequencies or supporting definition; a defining skeletal lesion or damage in at least 30% is not established.
